items.q: The Islamic calendar begins with this event.
The Islamic calendar follows this heavenly body.
The number of months in the Islamic year.
The first month of the Islamic year.
The month of fasting.
The number of sacred months.
The dynasty that ruled from Damascus after the Rightly Guided Caliphs.
The dynasty that ruled from Baghdad.
The city founded by the Abbasid caliph al-Mansur ⁨رحمة الله عليه⁩ in 145 AH / 762 CE.
The Muslim land in Spain.
The Muslim general who crossed into Spain in 92 AH / 711 CE.
The rock named after Tariq ibn Ziyad ⁨رحمة الله عليه⁩.
The Ayyubid sultan who freed Jerusalem in 583 AH / 1187 CE.
The battle that opened the way for Salah al-Din ⁨رحمة الله عليه⁩ to Jerusalem.
The empire that ruled from Istanbul.
The Ottoman sultan who conquered Constantinople in 857 AH / 1453 CE.
The famous "House of Wisdom" was in this city (meaning).
The Umayyad caliph known for justice, sometimes called the fifth Rightly Guided Caliph.
A hijri month lasts 29 days or this many.
The white marble tomb in Agra built by the Mughal emperor Shah Jahan ⁨رحمة الله عليه⁩.
The Rightly Guided Caliphs number this many.
The second of the Rightly Guided Caliphs, who began the hijri calendar.
The city of Egypt founded beside the Nile by our master 'Amr ibn al-'As ﵁.
The Umayyad capital in al-Andalus, famous for its great mosque.
The dynasty of Turkish slave-soldiers who ruled Egypt and Syria after the Ayyubids.
The city that became the Ottoman capital in 857 AH / 1453 CE.
The Muslim empire in India whose rulers built the Taj Mahal and the Red Fort.
The Moroccan traveller who visited China, India and Mali in the 8th century AH.
The city of our Beloved Prophet's ﷺ Hijrah, first capital of the Muslims.
The Iraqi city founded as a garrison town in about 14 AH / 635 CE, later a great centre of grammar.
The Companion called "the Sword of Allah" who led at Yarmuk.
The four sacred months.
The Umayyad state began with this caliph in 41 AH / 661 CE.
items.a: Mu'awiyah ibn Abi Sufyan ⁨(رِضْوَانُ اللَّهِ عَلَيْهِمَا)⁩

items.q: The year 41 AH, when our master al-Hasan ﵁ made peace, is called this.
The Umayyad prince who escaped and founded the Umayyad state in al-Andalus.
The capital of the Umayyads of al-Andalus.
The great mosque of Cordoba was begun by this ruler.
The Mongols sacked Baghdad in this year.
The battle where the Mamluks defeated the Mongols in 658 AH / 1260 CE.
The Mamluk sultan who led at 'Ayn Jalut.
The last Muslim kingdom in al-Andalus, which fell in 897 AH / 1492 CE.
The palace of the rulers of Granada.
The Umayyad caliph who built the Dome of the Rock.
The Umayyad caliph who built the great mosque of Damascus.
The Abbasid caliph famous in stories, who ruled 170-193 AH / 786-809 CE.
The Abbasid caliph who supported the House of Wisdom.
The Islamic university in Fez, among the oldest in the world, founded by a woman.
The woman who founded al-Qarawiyyin in 245 AH / 859 CE.
The great mosque and university of Cairo.
The Ottoman sultan called "the Lawgiver" (al-Qanuni).
The city where Salah al-Din ⁨رحمة الله عليه⁩ is buried.
The great mosque of Istanbul with six minarets, finished about 1026 AH / 1617 CE.
The battle of 15 AH / 636 CE in Syria where the Muslims defeated the Byzantines.
The battle in Iraq, about 15 AH / 636 CE, where the Muslims defeated the Persians.
The Companion who led the Muslims at al-Qadisiyyah.
Jerusalem was opened to the Muslims under this caliph, who came to receive its keys.
The governor of Egypt and Companion who led its opening in about 20 AH / 641 CE.
The second Ottoman siege of this city in 1094 AH / 1683 CE failed.
The Ayyubid dynasty is named after Salah al-Din's ⁨رحمة الله عليه⁩ father.
The Abbasid revolution began in this land in the east.
The scholar who wrote al-Muqaddimah on history and society.
The Imam who stood firm in the mihnah and was flogged.
items.a: Imam Ahmad ibn Hanbal ⁨رحمة الله عليه⁩

items.q: The Ottoman founder after whom the state is named.
The Mughal emperor who built the Taj Mahal.
The scholar who wrote "al-Bidayah wal-Nihayah".
The scholar of Khwarazm whose name gave us "algorithm".
The Muslim physician whose "Canon of Medicine" was taught for centuries (meaning).
The Abbasid caliph al-Musta'sim ⁨رحمة الله عليه⁩ was killed by the Mongols in this year.
The Muslim navy first won a great sea battle against the Byzantines under our master 'Uthman ﵁ at this battle.
The scholar of history who wrote Tarikh al-Rusul wal-Muluk.
Ibn Khaldun ⁨رحمة الله عليه⁩ was born in this city.
Ibn Khaldun's ⁨رحمة الله عليه⁩ idea of group feeling that builds states.
The traveller and judge of Tangier who journeyed for nearly 30 years.
The Andalusian traveller who wrote a famous Rihlah on his Hajj journey.
The Umayyad general who conquered Sind in 93 AH / 712 CE.
items.a: Muhammad ibn al-Qasim al-Thaqafi ⁨رحمة الله عليه⁩

items.q: The book of al-Baladhuri on the conquests of the lands.
The Seljuq vizier who founded the Nizamiyyah madrasahs.
The Seljuq victory over the Byzantines in 463 AH / 1071 CE.
The Seljuq sultan who won at Manzikert.
The Zengid ruler, master of Salah al-Din's ⁨رحمة الله عليه⁩ uncle Shirkuh, who united Syria.
The great history by Ibn al-Athir ⁨رحمة الله عليه⁩.
The book of al-Dhahabi ⁨رحمة الله عليه⁩ on the lives of the nobles.
The book of Ibn Khallikan ⁨رحمة الله عليه⁩ on the deaths of notables.
The Mughal emperor who commissioned al-Fatawa al-Hindiyyah (al-'Alamgiriyyah).
The Delhi sultanate's famous minaret built by Qutb al-Din Aybak.
The Mali king famous for his Hajj journey in 724 AH / 1324 CE.
The city of Mali famed for its manuscripts and scholars.
The Crusaders took Jerusalem in this year.
Salah al-Din ⁨رحمة الله عليه⁩ passed away in this year.
The English king who faced Salah al-Din ⁨رحمة الله عليه⁩ in the Third Crusade.
The Ottoman capital just before Istanbul.
The Umayyad Abd al-Rahman III ⁨رحمة الله عليه⁩ took this title in 316 AH / 929 CE.
The palace-city near Cordoba built by 'Abd al-Rahman III ⁨رحمة الله عليه⁩.
The Ayyubid sultan al-Kamil was the nephew of this great sultan.
The Mamluk sultan who ruled three times and built many works in Cairo, son of Qalawun ⁨رحمة الله عليه⁩.
items.a: al-Nasir Muhammad ibn Qalawun ⁨رحمة الله عليه⁩

items.q: The first Muslim naval expedition, to Cyprus in 28 AH / 649 CE, was led by this Companion governor of al-Sham.
The Sicilian city that was the capital of Muslim Sicily.
The Muslim dynasty of North Africa that took Sicily, from 212 AH / 827 CE.
The Abbasid caliph who founded Samarra as a new capital.
The Seljuq state of Anatolia whose capital was Konya.
items.a: The Sultanate of Rum (the Seljuqs of Rum)

items.q: The great hospital of Damascus founded by Nur al-Din Zangi ⁨رحمة الله عليه⁩.
The city in North Africa founded by 'Uqbah ibn Nafi' as a base.
The battle in 37 AH / 657 CE at which arbitration was agreed.
The Abbasid caliph in whose time the "mihnah" (trial) over the createdness of the Qur'an began.
The Abbasid caliph who ended the mihnah.
The Fatimid state, which founded Cairo, followed this creed.
Cairo was founded in this year.
Salah al-Din ⁨رحمة الله عليه⁩ ended Fatimid rule in Egypt in this year.
The book of al-Maqrizi ⁨رحمة الله عليه⁩ on the districts and history of Cairo.
The scholar of Tlemcen who wrote Nafh al-Tib, the great history of al-Andalus.
The Battle of Zallaqah in 479 AH / 1086 CE was won by this Almoravid leader.
The Almoravids are called this in Arabic.
The Almohads are called this in Arabic.
The battle in 609 AH / 1212 CE that weakened Muslim rule in al-Andalus.
The Ottoman sultan who took Egypt from the Mamluks in 923 AH / 1517 CE.
The year the Ottoman sultanate was ended.
The year the Ottoman caliphate was ended.
The Mughal dynasty was founded by this ruler in 932 AH / 1526 CE.
The battle of 932 AH / 1526 CE that founded Mughal rule.
The son of Babur ⁨رحمة الله عليه⁩ who lost, then won back, the Mughal throne.
The battle in 922 AH / 1516 CE at which Selim I ⁨رحمة الله عليه⁩ defeated the Mamluks in Syria.
The Umayyad general who reached the Pyrenees and fell at the battle the Arabs called Balat al-Shuhada'.
The battle of Balat al-Shuhada' (Tours/Poitiers) took place in this year.
The Abbasid caliph who moved the capital to Samarra was the brother of this caliph.
The Ottoman sultan who won at Mohacs in 932 AH / 1526 CE.
The Muslim empire of West Africa that came after Mali, with its capital at Gao.
The Songhay ruler who made the Hajj in 902 AH / 1497 CE and spread learning.
The history of West Africa written by 'Abd al-Rahman al-Sa'di ⁨رحمة الله عليه⁩ of Timbuktu.
The Muslim state of Central Asia whose ruler Ulugh Beg ⁨رحمة الله عليه⁩ built an observatory.
The Ottoman scholar who wrote Kashf al-Zunun and the Taqwim al-Tawarikh.
The Abbasid state began in this year.
The travel book of Ibn Battutah ⁨رحمة الله عليه⁩.
The Ottoman sultan who opened Constantinople was the son of this sultan.
The biographer of Salah al-Din ⁨رحمة الله عليه⁩ who was also his judge.
items.a: Baha' al-Din ibn Shaddad ⁨رحمة الله عليه⁩

items.q: The scholar who wrote "Tarikh al-Khulafa'" on the caliphs.
The Abbasid caliphate continued in name in this city after 656 AH.
The Mamluk sultan who won final victory over the Crusaders at Acre in 690 AH / 1291 CE.
The Mamluk sultan Baybars ⁨رحمة الله عليه⁩ won at 'Ayn Jalut alongside Qutuz ⁨رحمة الله عليه⁩ and later took this title.
The Timurid ruler who built the observatory in Samarqand.
The Ottoman scholar Hajji Khalifah ⁨رحمة الله عليه⁩ wrote this catalogue of books.
The Andalusian judge Ibn Rushd al-Jadd ⁨رحمة الله عليه⁩, grandfather of the philosopher, was a great jurist of this school.
The Ghaznavid sultan who campaigned into India and passed away in 421 AH / 1030 CE.
The scholar-scientist of Ghazni's court who wrote on India.
The Muslim geographer who made a world map for King Roger of Sicily.
The Muslim polymath of Basrah who wrote the Book of Optics.
The surgeon of al-Andalus who wrote al-Tasrif.
The Ottoman architect of the Süleymaniye Mosque.
The madrasah of Baghdad built by Nizam al-Mulk ⁨رحمة الله عليه⁩ and opened in 459 AH / 1067 CE.
The Andalusian scholar Ibn Hayyan ⁨رحمة الله عليه⁩ wrote this great history of al-Andalus.
The book on the Abbasid state and its scholars by al-Khatib al-Baghdadi ⁨رحمة الله عليه⁩.
The history of Damascus by Ibn 'Asakir ⁨رحمة الله عليه⁩.
The book of Ibn Taghri Birdi ⁨رحمة الله عليه⁩ on the kings of Egypt and Cairo.
The book of Ibn Iyas ⁨رحمة الله عليه⁩ on the history of Egypt to the Ottoman conquest.
The year the Mamluk sultan Qansuh al-Ghuri ⁨رحمة الله عليه⁩ fell at Marj Dabiq.
The last Mamluk sultan, hanged by the Ottomans at Bab Zuwaylah.
The book of Ibn al-Jawzi ⁨رحمة الله عليه⁩ on the history of kings and nations.
The Andalusian vizier and poet of Granada who was also a historian, author of al-Ihatah.
The Ayyubid-era scholar who wrote "Mir'at al-Zaman".
